item.title: Development of a low-level radio frequency system for remote in situ superconducting radio frequency cavity measurements and calibrations in conduction-cooling systems
item.description: arXiv:2611.33680v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We developed a low-level radio frequency (LLRF) system for superconducting radio frequency (SRF) cavity measurements in a conduction-cooling system. A voltage-controlled oscillator (VCO) was used in a phase-locked loop (PLL) to track the frequencies of SRF cavity modes. {\tt{Python}}-based software developed in-house controlled and monitored the system. By introducing an additional circulator and associated components, we developed an LLRF system enabling fully remote in situ SRF cavity measurements for the first time. This design also enables remote in situ calibrations. Hence, our LLRF system improves safety through fully remote operation and enhances measurement precision through in situ calibrations, with safety always taking priority. These calibrations are important for measurements in conduction-cooling systems because temperature stability and uniformity in these systems are poorer than those in convection-cooling systems using costly liquid helium and can vary over time and with environmental conditions.
item.dc:creator: C. Lim, K. Seol, S. E. Park, E. -S. Kim, E. Kako, S. Lee, B. R. Ko

item.title: A European high-capacity 100 MeV-per-nucleon heavy-ion facility for electronics irradiation based at CERN: Conceptual Design Report
item.description: arXiv:2608.26369v4 Announce Type: replace Abstract: This proposal presents a conceptual design for a European high-energy heavy-ion facility dedicated to electronics radiation-effects testing, directly addressing the critical challenges of global beam time shortages and energy limitations in existing facilities. Aligned with the HORIZON-CL4-2026-SPACE-03-85 call under Horizon Europe's Cluster 4 (Digital, Industry, and Space), the facility will enhance European sovereignty in space technology by providing approximately 1,900 additional hours of high-energy heavy-ion beam time annually, an increase of about 50% in the total heavy-ion beam time currently available in Europe for single-event-effect testing, and by extending the accessible ion energy range up to 100 MeV/nucleon, significantly improving penetration capabilities for state-of-the-art electronics testing. The facility will leverage CERN's ion injector chain up to the Low Energy Ion Ring (LEIR) synchrotron, adding a second ion source, a dedicated slow-extraction system, a transfer line and a user experimental area. The project timeline includes a pre-technical-design (pre-TDR) phase and a technical design phase leading to a Technical Design Report (TDR), followed by infrastructure and hardware production, installation, commissioning, and user operations. Funding is envisaged through a collaborative framework involving CERN and the European Union, with the aim of ensuring sustainable deployment and long-term operational success.
item.dc:creator: Edgar Cristopher Cort\'es Garc\'ia, Ruben Garc\'ia Alia, Matthew Alexander Fraser, Maciej Slupecki, Andreas Waets, Markus Widorski

item.title: Experimental Evidence for MeV Undulator Radiation Generated by Ultrarelativistic Positrons in a Periodically Bent Crystal
item.description: arXiv:2611.15542v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We report evidence for undulator radiation generated by ultrarelativistic positrons in a large-amplitude, long-period crystalline undulator. A pattern of Si$_3$N$_4$ stressors periodically bend the (110) planes of a Silicon crystal with a geometry measured independently by x-ray diffraction. Under planar alignment, the forward energy loss showed a localized excess at $6.8 \pm 0.3$~MeV, matching the predictions of simulations. Experimental results also indicate that an intense positron beam could make the undulator competitive in brilliance with state-of-the-art inverse-Compton gamma-ray sources.
